definitions.explanation: The physical location where building, road, or infrastructure construction is taking place.

examples.japanese: {工事現場|こうじげんば}に{入|はい}ってはいけない。
examples.english: You must not enter the construction site.

examples.japanese: {工事現場|こうじげんば}の{前|まえ}を{通|とお}るときはヘルメットが{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: You need a helmet when passing in front of the construction site.

examples.japanese: {夜間|やかん}の{工事現場|こうじげんば}から{大|おお}きな{騒音|そうおん}が{聞|き}こえて{近所|きんじょ}の{住民|じゅうみん}が{苦情|くじょう}を{出|だ}した。
examples.english: Loud noise from the nighttime construction site could be heard, and nearby residents filed complaints.

notes:
Composed of {工事|こうじ} (construction work) and {現場|げんば} (site, scene). A very common compound in daily life, as Japanese cities frequently have road and building construction. Signs reading {工事中|こうじちゅう} (under construction) are ubiquitous.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {工事現場|こうじげんば}で{働|はたら}く — to work at a construction site
- {工事現場|こうじげんば}の{安全|あんぜん}{管理|かんり} — construction site safety management
- {工事現場|こうじげんば}に{立|た}ち{入|い}り{禁止|きんし} — no trespassing at the construction site
- {工事現場|こうじげんば}{周辺|しゅうへん} — area around the construction site

RELATED TERMS:
- {建設現場|けんせつげんば} — building construction site (similar but emphasizes building rather than civil works)
- {工事中|こうじちゅう} — under construction
- {現場監督|げんばかんとく} — site supervisor; foreman
